specialties.why: Experts on an international IgG4-RD panel included rheumatology, and the disease is described as a multi-organ immune-mediated condition.
specialties.plain: A rheumatologist treats diseases where the immune system affects many organs. This fits IgG4-related disease.

specialties.why: Histopathology is described as key to diagnosis, and a consensus statement on IgG4-RD pathology exists.
specialties.plain: A pathologist studies tissue samples under a microscope. Tissue findings are key to diagnosing this disease.

specialties.subspecialty: Gastroenterology, nephrology, pulmonary medicine, ophthalmology, surgery
specialties.why: The disease can affect nearly any organ, and the international expert group spanned these specialties.
specialties.plain: Different organs can be affected, so you may need several kinds of specialists working together.

specialties.why: Allergy and immunology were among the subspecialties represented in the international IgG4-RD expert group.
specialties.plain: Allergy and immunology doctors study immune system diseases and may help with this condition.

centerCapabilities.text: Offers coordinated multidisciplinary work-up and follow-up, because nearly every organ system can be affected.
centerCapabilities.plain: The center has several kinds of specialists who work together on your care.

centerCapabilities.text: Has pathologists experienced in reading biopsies for IgG4-RD features such as storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis and IgG4-positive plasma cells.
centerCapabilities.plain: The center has pathologists who know how to read tissue samples for this disease.

centerCapabilities.text: Can distinguish IgG4-RD from malignant disease, infection and other autoimmune diseases, which can be challenging.
centerCapabilities.plain: The center can tell this disease apart from cancer, infection and other immune diseases.

centerCapabilities.text: Is familiar with the IgG4-RD Responder Index and the validated classification criteria used in international clinical studies.
centerCapabilities.plain: The center knows the standard tools doctors use to measure and classify this disease.

centerCapabilities.text: Takes part in patient registries or research, such as the multicenter IgG4-RD registry study registered in Japan.
centerCapabilities.plain: The center joins research or patient registries on this disease.

redFlags.text: A service that does not involve tissue (biopsy) pathology review in diagnosis may be a poor fit, since histopathology is key to diagnosing IgG4-RD.
redFlags.plain: Be careful if a service ignores tissue test results, because they are key to diagnosis.

redFlags.text: A single-specialty service with no access to other specialists may be a poor fit, as management needs multidisciplinary work-up.
redFlags.plain: Be careful if only one kind of doctor is involved and there is no team.

redFlags.text: A service unfamiliar with IgG4-RD may be a poor fit, as the disease mimics malignant, infectious and inflammatory disorders and greater awareness is needed.
redFlags.plain: Be careful if a service has not heard of this disease, because it can look like other conditions.

trialEligibility.text: Listings may ask how IgG4-RD was confirmed, such as by the 2019 ACR/EULAR classification criteria or biopsy histopathology.
trialEligibility.plain: Studies may ask how your diagnosis was confirmed, such as with a biopsy or standard criteria.

trialEligibility.text: Listings may ask about which organs are involved and whether the disease is the proliferative or the fibrotic type.
trialEligibility.plain: Studies may ask which organs are affected and what type of disease you have.

trialEligibility.text: Listings may ask about relapsing or refractory disease and past treatment history, since recurrent or refractory cases are common.
trialEligibility.plain: Studies may ask if the disease came back and what care you already had.

trialEligibility.text: Listings may use the IgG4-RD Responder Index to measure disease activity in clinical studies.
trialEligibility.plain: Studies may use a standard score to measure how active your disease is.

supportNeeds.text: GARD offers an information line for rare disease questions, plus pages on research participation, community and the diagnostic journey for IgG4-RD.
supportNeeds.plain: GARD has an information line and pages about research, community and getting diagnosed.

questions.text: Do you have a multidisciplinary team that coordinates care when IgG4-related disease affects several organs?
Do your pathologists review biopsies for IgG4-related disease features, and can you review outside biopsy slides?
How many people with IgG4-related disease do you see, and which organ specialists do you work with?
Do you use the IgG4-RD Responder Index or the ACR/EULAR classification criteria in your practice?
What diagnostic criteria or biopsy findings does this study require to confirm IgG4-related disease?
Does this study limit enrollment to certain organ involvement or to a fibrotic or proliferative type of disease?
Can you share information on IgG4-related disease research opportunities and patient communities?
